To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BH3‐ only molecules can rely on reticulum‐localized Bak to activate an apoptotic pathway that is independent of canonical Bak/Bax‐dependent mitochondrial signalling, and that this reticulum‐to‐mito‐chondrial signalling pathway is regulated by the ER‐stress response machinery IRE1a/TRAF2.
BH3‐Only molecules can activate an apoptotic pathway that relies on reticular Bak and the ER stress surveillance machinery IREα/TRAF2, independently of the canonical mitochondrial gateway.
BH3‐ only molecules can induce cytochrome release from mitochondria in the exclusive presence, at the endoplasmatic reticulum, of Bak.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the endoplasmatic reticulum (or ER) in the induction of apoptosis.
the mechanisms of apoptosis, a process of programmed cell death essential to the development and homeostasis of multicellular organisms, and the mechanisms by which it is controlled.
the mechanisms that regulate cell death and survival.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mitochondrial Bak is the primary and most important mediator of apoptosis in the presence of BH3‐only proteins and that the ER‐localized Bak can also contribute to this process, but only in specific circumstances.
the ER‐to‐mitchondria signalling route is able to induce cytosolic cytochrome c accumulation and apoptosis independently of mitochondrial Bak and Bax.
BH3‐Only proteins can induce mitochondrial apoptosis in cells expressing exclusively ER‐localized Bak.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endoplasmatic reticular localization of Bak, which is a pro‐apoptotic Bcl2‐family member, is enough to induce apoptosis when the cell is stimulated by BH3‐ only molecules.
BH3‐Only molecules can induce apoptosis in cells that express only ER‐Bak, but that calcium release and IRE1/TRAF2 are required for this to occur.
BH3‐ only molecules in the exclusive absence of mitochondrial Bak and Bax can activate a Bak‐mediated mitochondrial apoptosis in the presence of endoplamic reticular Bak.
The main takeaway from our work is that

BH3‐Only proteins, such as BimEL and Noxa, can induce apoptosis in the exclusive presence and activity of Bak in endoplamic reticulum membranes, independently of the mitochondrial localization of Bak and Bax.

reticular Bak may act independently of mitochondrial Bax to activate an ER–mitochondrial signalling pathway that is able to induce cytoplasmic cytochrome c and apoptosis in response to BH3‐only stimuli, thus revealing a layer of complexity in the control of cell death.

BH3‐ only molecules can rely on reticulum‐localized Bak to induce mitochondrial apoptosis independently of its mitochondrial counterpart, and that this process involves the endoplasmatic reticulum stress surveillance machinery.
